correctness.rationale: For H=G[A], p marked vertices with marked degree>=2 satisfy p<=e. Let Q be unmarked vertices with at least two marked neighbors. The induced J on A union Q has >=e+2q edges and m+q vertices; beta(J)<=beta(G) and >=1 component imply q<=m-1+beta(G)-e. Thus p+q<=m-1+beta(G), accounting for all >=2 traces, with <=m singleton and <=1 empty. Sharp connected triangular cacti have exactly 3c+(m-2c-1)+m+1=2m+c distinct traces, and beta=c. Direct checker executed 2,097,151 exhaustive small graph/mark cases and 81 cactus witnesses.

value.rationale: Independent cycle number is a structural distance-to-forest parameter. The result identifies an exact cost of one additional open-adjacency type for each permitted cycle, and supplies equality witnesses simultaneously for all stable sizes, strengthening asymptotic neighborhood-complexity statements into a sharp finite-model-theoretic type bound. In contrast to a routine unmotivated single-value computation, it gives a uniform theorem plus extremal constructions for an entire natural graph hierarchy.
